research_question: In people with multiple sclerosis, what is the effect of memory rehabilitation compared with a control condition on subjective memory functioning at the intermediate follow-up timepoint (approximately 1 to 6 months post-treatment)?
control_label: Control condition (usual care, waitlist, or active control)
outcome_description: Subjective memory functioning (self-reported memory problems or memory capabilities in daily life assessed via standardized questionnaires or self-report rating scales, such as the Everyday Memory Questionnaire [EMQ], Memory Functioning Questionnaire [MFQ], or Prospective and Retrospective Memory Questionnaire [PRMQ]) assessed at an intermediate follow-up timepoint (approximately 1 to 6 months post-treatment).
positive_direction: A positive effect size indicates greater subjective memory functioning (or fewer reported everyday memory failures/complaints) in the memory rehabilitation group compared with the control group.
search_queries: multiple sclerosis memory rehabilitation trial subjective memory
multiple sclerosis cognitive rehabilitation randomized controlled trial self reported memory
multiple sclerosis memory training controlled comparison memory questionnaire
inclusion_criteria: Empirical studies involving adults diagnosed with multiple sclerosis receiving a memory rehabilitation or cognitive intervention aimed at improving memory.
Inclusion of a comparison or control condition (such as usual care, waitlist, sham, or an active comparator).
Reporting of quantitative data on subjective (self-reported) memory functioning assessed at an intermediate follow-up timepoint (approximately 1 to 6 months post-treatment).
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study (systematic reviews, meta-analyses, narrative reviews, editorials, conference abstracts without full data, opinion pieces, or theoretical papers are excluded).
No comparison between a memory rehabilitation intervention and a control condition (e.g., uncontrolled pre-post studies or case reports).
No quantitative outcome data permitting effect size calculation for subjective memory (means and standard deviations, standard errors, t/F-values, or exact p-values).

Completely unrelated to multiple sclerosis, or reporting only objective cognitive test performance or other non-subjective memory domains without any self-reported/subjective memory questionnaire data.
moderators_to_extract: Control group type (passive/usual care/waitlist vs. active comparator)
Rehabilitation modality (individual vs. group; computerized vs. clinician-led compensatory/restorative)
Intermediate follow-up duration (exact weeks or months within the 1 to 6 month window)
Multiple sclerosis clinical phenotype (relapsing-remitting vs. progressive vs. mixed)
Specific subjective memory outcome instrument used (e.g., EMQ, MFQ, PRMQ)
